items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: a friend of mine, Jerry Dodgion, a wonderful saxophonist

ctx.x: It’s good for both of them. It makes the piano player work harder.

Like I told my arranging class, even in the class, show no mercy. I mean you’re there, you’re putting your stuff out there on the line, but even as a writer you don’t write down, you never write down. You just write. And it’s the orchestra or band’s job — my music is difficult play but a friend of mine, Jerry Dodgion, a wonderful saxophonist and also has one of the greatest attitudes in the world, and is also a wonderful writer. He writes like one chart a year but it’s a good one, but he said your music is…
Tell me about working with Joe Williams.
